business_problem: Montgomery County Food Bank had a lean budget and increasing operational workloads: staff sorted non-food inventory, drivers accumulated overtime, partner agencies paid retail prices for supplemental food, and donor, email, and volunteer records were split across platforms.
solution_summary: Montgomery County Food Bank uses Claude across sourcing, fleet operations, finance, and donor communications. Staff use Claude in Excel to compare a partner agency's purchases with the food bank's at-cost prices, Claude to analyze inventory exports and routing and shift patterns, and Claude Fable to compare Form 990s and prepare reports. Claude Cowork supports a multi-step donor follow-up workflow; Claude for Outlook drafts personalized thank-yous, while Fable helps match records across donor, email, and volunteer platforms. Staff use Claude Opus and Sonnet for daily work, Fable for harder strategy and data tasks, and Claude in Chrome for form building and website edits. Inputs include operational exports, purchase and peer-filing data, and donor records; outputs include buying and scheduling decisions, dashboards, and individualized messages. The bank keeps donor personal data out of Claude.

data_flow: Purchase records are compared in Claude in Excel with food-bank at-cost prices; inventory exports and fleet routing and shift patterns are analyzed to guide sorting and schedules. Form 990 filings and operational data produce board and event-level comparisons. Claude Fable matches records across donor, email, and volunteer platforms, while gift details feed personalized Outlook drafts and a Cowork workflow for follow-up.
business_outcome: Claude helped reduce driver and warehouse overtime, lower partner-agency food costs, speed reporting, and give staff more capacity for food distribution and donor stewardship. The bank reports that reduced operating costs let it deliver more food while keeping overhead near 4%.
